title: Recheck eager improvements under production graph execution
applies_when: A change saves Python dispatch or launch overhead, uses a runtime override, or routes on tensor shape while production uses compilation or CUDA graph replay.
lesson: Compare baseline and candidate in the same production execution mode and verify the changed path executes there. Graph replay can remove the CPU work that dominated an eager experiment. Report startup and capture separately from steady-state latency. When dispatch needs the logical phase or valid row count, verify it still receives that information under padded or compiled execution. Before a static backend reorder, sweep the reached serving batch/shape portfolio in production mode; a batch-1 win can become a larger-batch regression, and a static selector may not observe runtime token count.
avoid_when: An eager diagnostic can isolate a mechanism but cannot establish the sign of a graph-mode improvement. Do not add graph-specific machinery to a workload that only uses eager execution.

evidence.note: PyTorch documents fixed replay arguments, reduced CPU overhead and omitted CPU work during replay. Production routing and performance conclusions remain candidate-specific hypotheses.

Author-reported RTX 5060 Laptop/SM120 W4A16 case: eager/model gains did not survive the default graph serving-batch sweep; the PR is closed unmerged. This is a public report, not our independent reproduction, portable speedup or general hardware ranking.
The proposed static reorder uses compute capability, activation dtype and weight K, not runtime M. Source scope only; author-reported graph/E2E outcomes remain separate.
